presentation.summary: Reach Silo through your tailnet without opening public ports.
presentation.description_markdown: Runs a separate Tailscale node on the API host and every proxy. Exposes the native, Jellyfin and Audiobookshelf listeners over HTTPS on your tailnet only. Optionally, people whose device reaches Silo over Tailscale sign in as the device's owner with no password; your tailnet policy decides who can and with which role.
presentation.setup_markdown: Requires Silo's network-access plugin support, one API host, and MagicDNS plus HTTPS certificates enabled in Tailscale. Save an optional reusable auth key for automatic enrollment across proxies, then select Connect in Settings > Network Access. Otherwise use the authorization URL shown for each host. To let people sign in with their Tailscale identity, turn on Tailscale under Settings > Sign-in > Network sign-in.

capabilities.description: Sign in as the owner of the device a request came from over Tailscale.

global_config_schema.title: Tailscale
global_config_schema.description: Enrollment settings shared by all hosts. Each host retains its own node identity.

fields.label: Hostname
fields.description: The API host uses this exact hostname. Proxy nodes use <hostname>-proxy-<node id> to keep each node distinct.

fields.label: Auth key
fields.description: Optional Tailscale auth key. Use a reusable key for multiple hosts; leave empty for interactive enrollment.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Optional comma-separated tags, for example tag:silo. Tags must be authorized by your tailnet policy or auth key. Applies to the API host and all proxies.

fields.label: Who can sign in

options.label: Anyone who can reach Silo over Tailscale
options.description: Every untagged device that reaches this server, including people you share it with.

options.label: Only people granted siloserver.org/cap/silo
options.description: A grant in your tailnet policy decides who may sign in and with which role.

fields.description: Who may sign in to Silo with their Tailscale identity once Tailscale is turned on under Settings > Sign-in. Either way, a siloserver.org/cap/silo grant with {"role":"admin"} or {"role":"user"} sets the person's Silo role.

fields.label: Subnet routers

options.label: Can sign in
options.description: A subnet router signs in as its owner, like any other device. Machines on the LAN behind it keep their own addresses and get no Tailscale identity.

options.label: Cannot sign in
options.description: For tailnets where a router rewrites forwarded LAN traffic to its own Tailscale address, which would let everyone behind it sign in as its owner.

fields.description: Whether devices that route a subnet into the tailnet can sign in with their Tailscale identity. Exit nodes are not affected.
